title: Price of Unknown Rare-Cell Intensity for ATE Estimation versus Honest Intervals
banked_reason: D0.5.G paper-score ceiling 6.4 below field threshold 7.4; sound same-instance result, no scoped field-tier repair.
gap_reasons: The interval contribution remains localized to that single numerical design and does not characterize when a positive price occurs
the condition a lambda_U <= 1/5 is only a sufficient MSE region rather than a sharp phase boundary

The claimed data-only attainment is asymptotic minimax-envelope attainment implemented through exhaustive finite-grid selectors with unspecified ledger constants, not a practically executable or finite-sample optimal method

These restrictions, the absence of an application, and reliance on external arithmetic artifacts for the headline numerical gap limit the leading-journal score despite the genuine field-level decision-theoretic result
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a same-instance decision-criterion separation: zero unknown-intensity minimax MSE price and a certified positive honest connected-interval price above 0.03480. The numerical certificate was independently rerun, and the decision and math panels passed without findings. The D0.5 cold referee nevertheless capped the delivered paper at incremental because the interval result is localized to one design and the MSE condition is sufficient rather than a sharp phase boundary; no bounded field-tier repair remained.
tldr: A full-population ATE can retain root-sample-size sensitivity to a covariate stratum even when only finitely many treated outcomes are observed there. The local experiment is Gaussian for ordinary cells and marked Poisson for the rare treated cell. On every symmetric connected rare-risk class satisfying \(a\lambda_U\leq1/5\), an intensity-free endpoint-posterior estimator has exactly zero unknown-intensity minimax MSE price. At the single legal interior design \(c=8\), \(\sigma=1/4\), \(\mathcal Q=[1/4,3/4]\), and \(\Lambda=[1/2,4/5]\), where \(a\lambda_U=1/5\), an outward-Arb certificate simultaneously gives \(\Delta_M=0\) and connected \(90\%\) interval-length price \(\Delta_I>0.03480\). The proved two-sided experiment transfer and uniform pilot-selected procedures attain the corresponding limits from the observed causal data without estimating the unlearnable coefficient \(d\).
gap: Limited-overlap ATE theory identifies local cell counts as the source of poor Gaussian inference, and decision theory provides minimax estimation and expected-length duality, but neither literature determines how an unknown finite count intensity changes different decision criteria for an untrimmed causal target.
fill: The project derives a two-sided Gaussian--marked-Poisson transfer, proves an exact zero MSE price on a connected low-intensity region, certifies a strictly positive honest connected-interval price at a distinct legal design, and exposes uniform pilot-selected finite-data attainment as the load-bearing open construction.
